newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper ends sharply up on good sentiment.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper ends sharply up on good sentiment.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended sharply up in active trading on Tuesday on good market sentiment, but profit-taking pushed prices from their highs, traders said.
They said overnight gains on the London Metal Exchange (LME) improved market sentiment but enthusiastic profit-taking emerged at higher levels later in the session after two days of heavy gains.
The most active May 1997 contract ended at 22,580 yuan ($2,723) per tonne, rising 480 yuan. It opened at an intraday low of 22,450 and hit a high of 22,700.
March rose 190 to 22,310, April 380 to 22,510, June 460 to 22,560, July 450 to 22,550 and August 360 to 22,560.
Combined volume rose sharply to 103,530 tonnes from 12,120.
Copper opened higher and moved at high levels before profit-taking pushed prices sharply down late in the session but still up from Monday's close.
"Stop loss buying early in the session was the major factor for the rises, but it will be very difficult for further sharp rises in the next few days," one trader said.
"Open interest fell sharply today, indicating investors are not very optimistic about short-term market trends," he said.
Traders said copper price movements on the LME would be the main factor influencing the Shanghai market in days to come.
"Shanghai copper is likely to remain at high levels if the LME continues to move strongly, otherwise we will see a technical correction soon," a second trader said.
Aluminium ended down on profit-taking. March fell 40 yuan to 15,560, April 50 to 15,850 and May 50 to 15,950.
Combined volume fell to 1,290 tonnes from 2,070.
